You're prepping backlog-refinement notes for a Salesforce PWA Kit storefront (Zimmermann) FED Lead, for Jira ticket SFCC-836 "Icon and Text PWA Kit Component". Read-only research — you are not writing to Jira or Confluence.

SHARED GROUND TRUTH (cite, don't re-derive):
- Today is 2026-09-03. Real Sprint 4 runs 2026-08-24–2026-09-07 (active now); Sprint 5 runs 2026-09-07–2026-09-21. The repo's .docs/memory/sprintScope.md is CONFIRMED STALE — judge this ticket on its own Jira status/fields.
- Decomposition pattern (Confluence 04.71): a Contentful+PWA-Kit component gets TWO stories. SFCC-835 "Icon and Text Contentful Component Model" is this ticket's sibling content-model story — fetch it too.
- Figma 04.7 Component Inventory (re-checked live today) has no "Icon and Text" row — check the ticket for a direct Figma link instead.
- New Zimmermann components live at overrides/app/components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/<camelCase>/, each with a theme recipe registered in overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts. Check overrides/app/components/ui-kits/ for current state — an icon+text atom/molecule may already partially exist (e.g. check zimmIcon).
- No-mocking rule: production paths must consume live Contentful data via @salesforce/commerce-sdk-react-equivalent Contentful hooks, not hardcoded fixtures — but Storybook/Vitest may reasonably stub the shape while SFCC-835's real schema isn't installed yet.

DO THIS:
1. Fetch the full ticket: jira_get_issue(issue_key='SFCC-836', fields='summary,description,status,issuelinks,comment,attachment,parent', comment_limit=20).
2. Fetch SFCC-835 the same way for the sequencing check — can SFCC-836 realistically start against a stubbed shape in parallel with SFCC-835, or does it need SFCC-835's real schema decided first?
3. Check overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon/ briefly for what already exists to reuse.
4. Apply the seven-point sizing lens: (1) any FE impact? (2) is the requirement clear enough to size? (3) which surfaces does it touch — where does this render (check the ticket, cross-reference SFCC-835's answer)? (4) design/Figma dependencies? (5) API/backend dependencies (depends on SFCC-835's Contentful schema landing)? (6) pure FE, shared FE/BE, or needs architecture input? (7) size now, or need clarification first?
5. Read for the four standing axes: behaviour, desktop/mobile, a11y (icon needs an accessible name/alt from the content model — confirm SFCC-835's schema actually carries this field), data — flag anything genuinely unclear.
6. Design dependency: does a design exist?
7. Altitude: BAs own component-decomposition questions, devs own atomic/build questions.

OUTPUT, in this exact shape:
- One-line plain-language summary
- Seven lens answers
- Four axes, flagging what's unclear
- Design status + source
- The SFCC-835/SFCC-836 sequencing verdict (can they run in parallel, or is this genuinely blocked on 835 first)
- Specific questions to raise, each tagged with who should answer it
- One-line readiness call

Be concrete, don't editorialize past what the data supports, and say plainly what you couldn't check.

This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. - dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/skills/zimmerMANNSprinter

For the ceremonies. Reads the board and the docs, gives you what you need to walk into the room
with, and never speaks on your behalf without you seeing it first.

**Intended model: Sonnet 5 at maximum effort.**

**Sources: Jira and Confluence.** Trello is named in the original spec but **there is no MCP
connector for it and none in the registry** — it is outside what this skill can see. Say so rather
than implying coverage.

**No overthinking. Straightforward. Work with what we have, not with what we lack.** Run a sanity
check on anything before it goes to a colleague — a question raised at the wrong altitude costs
more than one not raised.

---

## Modes

`refine <keys>` · `plan <sprint>` · `standup` · `retro <sprint>` · `prep <invite>`

Any mode accepts a pasted meeting invite as extra context.

---

## `refine <keys>` — backlog refinement

For each story, run the sizing lens and the four axes. Output is **a question list you can take
into the room**, not a verdict.

**Several keys at once: fan out**, one general-purpose agent per ticket — each reading its own Jira
issue, its linked design and any related Confluence, and returning the lens and axes for that story
alone. Reconcile them yourself. One key: read it sequentially, no agents. Scale to the need.

Do not use the `zm-*` agents here. They are build-loop roles and have nothing to do with refinement.

### The seven-point sizing lens

1. Is there any **front-end impact**?
2. Is the requirement **clear enough to size**?
3. **Which surfaces** does it touch — PWA Kit / React, Contentful, SFCC integration, checkout,
   account, PDP/PLP, CMS-rendered?
4. Are there **design / Figma dependencies**?
5. Are there **API / backend dependencies**?
6. Is this **pure FE**, a shared FE/BE change, or does it need **architecture input**?
7. Can we **size now**, or do we need clarification first?

### The four standing axes

Every story gets read for: **behaviour · desktop/mobile · a11y · data.**

Those four are where the ambiguity usually hides, and they are the questions worth asking while
the BA and the designer are still in the room.

### Design dependency — call it out explicitly

A story blocked on design componentization **cannot be picked up**, however well it is written.
Check the linked Figma: does the design exist, is it current rather than archived, are all variants
and states drawn. Flag every story where the answer is no, by name.

This is the one that silently sinks a sprint commitment. It has happened before.

### Altitude

**BAs work at the component level; devs take the atomic level.** Pitch each question for whoever
owns the answer. A question about atom decomposition is not a refinement question — it is a
build decision, and raising it here wastes the room's time.

### Output

Per story: the seven answers, the four axes with anything unclear flagged, design status, and
**the specific questions to raise, with who should answer each.** Then a one-line readiness call —
sizeable now, or blocked on X.

---

## `plan <sprint>` — sprint planning

For each candidate story:

- **Refined?** Has it been through refinement, and did anything come out unresolved?
- **Has acceptance criteria?** Actual ACs, not a description.
- **Design signed off?** Not "design exists" — signed off.
- **What does it depend on?** Other stories, another squad, an integration, a decision.
- **What is blocking it right now?**

Then a **sequencing suggestion**: design-dependent work last, shared-component work first, and
anything that unblocks another story ahead of the thing it unblocks. State the reasoning so it can
be argued with.

**Capacity and assignment stay out.** The skill does not know who is on leave, who is carrying
support, or how the team feels about the load. That is the room's conversation.

---

## `standup`

Derive the factual half. Ask for the rest.

**What you did** — commits authored since the last standup, PRs opened, reviewed or merged, Jira
transitions on your tickets.

```bash
git log --author="$(git config user.email)" --since="yesterday" --oneline
gh pr list --author "@me" --state all --limit 10 --json number,title,state,updatedAt
```

Plus Jira transitions on tickets assigned to you.

**What you are doing** — from the tickets in progress and the branch you are on.

**What is blocking you** — **ask.** Do not infer it. A PR sitting unreviewed for two days might be
a blocker or might be fine, and only you know which.

Keep it short. This is a two-minute update, not a report.

---

## `retro <sprint>`

Factual input to a human conversation. Not an opinion about how the sprint went.

- **Committed versus shipped** — what went into the sprint, what closed.
- **Carried over** — and how many sprints each has now carried.
- **Reopened** — anything that went back to In Progress after being called done.
- **Time in review** — how long PRs sat before first review and before merge.
- **Build run artefacts** — anything under `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/`: rework rounds
  per step, what the Scorer kept returning, what a loop could not verify.

Present the numbers and stop. **Do not editorialise.** The team decides what any of it means, and
a retro pre-loaded with conclusions steers toward what is measurable rather than what mattered.

---

## `prep <invite>`

Paste any meeting invite — ceremony or not. Alignment calls, TNL sessions, vendor sessions,
design reviews.

Read the **agenda, the attendees and the stated objectives**, then prepare for that specific
meeting rather than a generic template:

- What is this meeting actually for, in one line
- What each attendee will want from you
- What you need to know before walking in — from Jira, Confluence, the codebase
- **The questions worth asking**, and who to ask each
- Anything you should have an answer ready for
- Anything genuinely outside your remit, named as such

---

## Writing to Jira

Estimates, comments, transitions and AC edits all go on a shared board under your name.

**Draft it, show it, write it on your explicit go.** Never before.

And because it is outward-facing, the phrasing rule applies: **where the owner is senior or
lateral, phrase it as a question, never a directive.** Ask confirmatorily. Before anything posts,
count the asks — a comment that tags one person five times reads as hiding behind their authority.

---

## Output

**"ELI5 but I'm the FED Lead"** register — not dumbed down, but without jargon that gets in the
way. Lead with the consequence.

Put decisions to Marcel **one at a time, using AskUserQuestion.** Never a wall of choices.

Where the output is a message to a person — Teams, a Jira comment, an email — write it in **natural
human language without sacrificing the technical accuracy.** No em-dashes. No AI tells. It should
read as though he wrote it, because he is the one sending it.

---

## Hard rules

- **Never write to Jira or Confluence without an explicit go.**
- **Never invent an acceptance criterion, an estimate, or a dependency.** If it is not in the
  ticket, it is a question, not a finding.
- **Never claim Trello coverage.** It is not connected.
- **Never model capacity or assign work.** Not the skill's call.
- **Never editorialise a retro.**
- **Say what you could not check.** A ticket you could not read, a Confluence page that 404s, a
  design link that is dead — each is itself worth raising.

7	const ZIMM_CONTACT_ICON_ROW_RECIPE = 'ZimmContactIconRow';
8	
9	// Figma: Icon-list has pt-4px (alias/space/100) above it and 4px internal gap between icons.
10	// hrefs are typically sourced from Contentful (FooterConfigEntry, HPC-034) by the caller. Until
11	// that integration lands, absent hrefs render each icon as a non-interactive but labelled
12	// <span> — visible in the layout and announced by screen readers, but absent from the tab
13	// order. See the inline note on the fallback branch below for the full a11y reasoning. When a
14	// href arrives it switches to a live <a>, no other changes needed.
15	// Fallback labels for a footerConfig entry authored before phoneLabel/whatsAppLabel/
16	// emailLabel existed — kept here, not duplicated as a second uiCopy source, since
17	// footerConfig is this row's one real content source (see footerConfig.js's field comment).
18	const DEFAULT_PHONE_LABEL = 'Call us';
19	const DEFAULT_WHATSAPP_LABEL = 'WhatsApp';
20	const DEFAULT_EMAIL_LABEL = 'Email us';
21	
22	type ZimmContactIconRowProps = {
23	  phoneHref?: string; // locale-aware tel: href
24	  phoneLabel?: string; // Contentful footerConfig.phoneLabel — falls back to DEFAULT_PHONE_LABEL
25	  whatsAppHref?: string; // WhatsApp URL
26	  whatsAppLabel?: string; // Contentful footerConfig.whatsAppLabel — falls back to DEFAULT_WHATSAPP_LABEL
27	  emailHref?: string; // mailto: address
28	  emailLabel?: string; // Contentful footerConfig.emailLabel — falls back to DEFAULT_EMAIL_LABEL
29	};
30	
31	type ContactLink = { href?: string; label: string; icon: 'phone' | 'whatsapp' | 'email' };
32	
33	/**
34	 * True when following the href would navigate away from the storefront.
35	 *
36	 * Takes `string | undefined` rather than `string` so the caller does not need an `as string` to
37	 * satisfy it inside an isSafeHref branch. isSafeHref returns a plain boolean, which carries no
38	 * narrowing, and a `href is string` predicate would be unsound — an unsafe value like
39	 * `javascript:void(0)` is a string that returns false, so the else branch would narrow to
40	 * `undefined` incorrectly. An absent href never leaves the site, so `?? ''` is the honest answer.
41	 *
42	 * Derived from the scheme rather than keyed to a channel name: tel: and mailto: hand off to the
43	 * OS dialer or mail client and never navigate, so a target on them does nothing. An http(s)
44	 * channel — WhatsApp today — is a real cross-origin navigation and opens in a new tab so a
45	 * shopper mid-browse does not lose the site. Any future http(s) channel inherits this without
46	 * another edit here.
47	 */
48	const leavesTheSite = (href: string | undefined): boolean => /^https?:/i.test(href ?? '');
49	
50	/**
51	 * Contact channel icon row (phone / WhatsApp / email). Extracted from the footer so it can be
52	 * reused anywhere a storefront needs the same channels — nothing here is footer-specific.
53	 *
54	 * @param props see ZimmContactIconRowProps
55	 */
56	export const ZimmContactIconRow = ({
57	  phoneHref,
58	  phoneLabel,
59	  whatsAppHref,
60	  whatsAppLabel,
61	  emailHref,
62	  emailLabel,
63	}: ZimmContactIconRowProps) => {
64	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_CONTACT_ICON_ROW_RECIPE, {});
65	  const { t } = useUiCopy();
66	  // WCAG 3.2.5 — a link that opens a new tab has to say so in its accessible name.
67	  const newTabSuffix = t('contact_icon_row.assistive_msg.opens_in_new_tab', ' — opens in a new tab');
68	  const links: ContactLink[] = [
69	    { href: phoneHref, label: phoneLabel ?? DEFAULT_PHONE_LABEL, icon: 'phone' },
70	    { href: whatsAppHref, label: whatsAppLabel ?? DEFAULT_WHATSAPP_LABEL, icon: 'whatsapp' },
71	    { href: emailHref, label: emailLabel ?? DEFAULT_EMAIL_LABEL, icon: 'email' },
72	  ];
73	  return (
74	    <chakra.div __css={styles.row}>
75	      {links.map(({ href, label, icon }) =>
76	        // isSafeHref, not a truthiness check: these typically arrive from Contentful, so a
77	        // javascript:/data:/protocol-relative value would otherwise be rendered straight onto
78	        // an anchor. Rejected values fall through to the span below, which is already the
79	        // correct treatment for "no usable destination".
80	        isSafeHref(href) ? (
81	          <chakra.a
82	            key={icon}
83	            href={href}
84	            // rel is explicit rather than relying on target="_blank" implying noopener: that is
85	            // browser default behaviour, not a guarantee, and noreferrer also stops the
86	            // storefront URL leaking to the third party.
87	            {...(leavesTheSite(href) ? { target: '_blank', rel: 'noopener noreferrer' } : {})}
88	            aria-label={leavesTheSite(href) ? `${label}${newTabSuffix}` : label}
89	            __css={styles.iconLink}
90	          >
91	            <ZimmIcon type={icon} size="md" aria-hidden={true} />
92	          </chakra.a>
93	        ) : (
94	          // Fallback for a channel with no usable destination — either the field is absent, or
95	          // isSafeHref rejected the value. Both reach here, and both want the same treatment.
96	          // NON-INTERACTIVE but PERCEIVABLE:
97	          //   - <span>: no href, no tabIndex, so nothing promises an action that cannot be
98	          //     performed (avoids the WCAG 2.4.4 / 3.2.4 false affordance).
99	          //   - labelled, not aria-hidden: ZimmIcon emits role="img" + aria-label, so screen
100	          //     reader users learn the channel exists instead of getting silence (avoids the
101	          //     1.1.1 information loss the previous aria-hidden caused).
102	          // Not dead code: contact channels are optional per storefront, so a locale that
103	          // supplies only e.g. email still renders the other two icons this way.
104	          <chakra.span key={icon} __css={styles.iconLink}>
105	            <ZimmIcon type={icon} size="md" aria-label={label} />
106	          </chakra.span>
107	        ),
108	      )}
109	    </chakra.div>
110	  );
111	};

content.text:
## SFCC-836 "Icon and Text — PWA Kit Component" — Backlog Refinement Notes

**One-line summary:** SFCC-836 is the PWA Kit half of a new reusable "Icon and Text" tile component (2, 3, or 4 tiles horizontal, or vertical — each tile is icon + bold heading + body copy, entirely Contentful-driven); it's currently only evidenced live as the "Zimmermann Benefits" row on Cart, both it and its Contentful sibling SFCC-835 are PO-approved but still sitting in **Tech design**, and the icon-asset question alone is concrete enough to block a confident size today (the mockup's icons don't exist in the current icon set).

---

### Seven-point sizing lens

1. **FE impact?** Yes — net-new component, and possibly the first real component registered through this repo's Contentful Experience Builder path (see lens 6).
2. **Clear enough to size?** Not fully. Both tickets are narrative user-story descriptions (As a/I want/so that + prose) — no bulleted Acceptance Criteria came back in the fields fetched. Several load-bearing specifics are undefined (see axes below).
3. **Which surfaces?** PWA Kit/React + Contentful, confirmed. The only *evidenced* placement is Cart ("Zimmermann Benefits" — matches parent epic SFCC-11 "Cart"). Both tickets say "examples of where this is used" (plural) but both attach the identical single Cart screenshot — no second placement is actually shown yet.
4. **Design/Figma dependencies?** Yes — see Design status below.
5. **API/backend dependencies?** Yes, entirely Contentful-side (SFCC-835's content type). No SFCC/commerce API dependency found.
6. **Pure FE / shared / architecture input?** Shared FE + Contentful pairing, following an already-proven pattern in this codebase — presentational organism receiving props (e.g. `ZimmSubscribeSection` takes `heading`/`body` as props, doesn't fetch), with actual fetching done at page/container level via `useContentful`/`useContentfulClient`. No new data-flow architecture needed. One genuinely fresh piece: `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/definitions.ts` (the Experience Builder component registry) is currently **empty** — "every experiences/*.tsx component was removed... never had a real @cf-register'd component" — so if this is meant to register there, it's among the first real ones. Worth a heads-up, not a blocker.
7. **Size now or clarify first?** Clarify first. Rough shape is fine for a planning conversation; not sizeable to a confident point estimate today.

---

### Four standing axes

- **Behaviour:** N tiles of icon + bold heading + body, Contentful-driven. SFCC-836 explicitly says it "handles empty/error states" but neither ticket says what that state looks like. Unclear whether tile count is dynamic (however many entries get linked) or a fixed authored choice, and whether tiles are ever clickable — no href field is mentioned anywhere and neither mockup shows a link affordance.
- **Desktop/mobile:** Ticket claims responsive requirements are "met" but no mobile mockup or breakpoint behaviour is described or attached. Unclear whether "vertical layout" *is* the mobile answer or a separate authorable option orthogonal to breakpoint.
- **A11y:** The existing `ZimmIcon` atom (`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon/index.tsx`) hard-requires either `aria-hidden={true}` or a real `aria-label` string per icon — there's no third option in its prop type. SFCC-835's description names only icon/heading/body as fields; no accessible-name/alt field is mentioned. Icon-decorative-with-heading-as-label is a reasonable guess but isn't a stated decision anywhere.
- **Data:** Fully Contentful-driven, no hardcoding — explicit and agreed in both tickets. But the icon field's shape is a real, evidenced gap: the mockup icons (delivery truck, package/gift box, padlock) do **not** exist among `ZimmIcon`'s current types — its `ZimmIconType` union (34 Figma-spec icons + 3 footer-only extras: phone/whatsapp/email) has no shipping/package/lock icon. SFCC-835 needs to decide whether to extend that closed, spec-tied enum or model the icon as a Contentful asset reference instead — these are materially different builds for SFCC-836.

---

### Design status + source

Both tickets link the same Figma node: design-system file `wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm`, node-id `40003038-130551`. Checked live via Figma MCP just now — it resolves inside the file's single "UI KIT / design system package" page to a text layer reading **"ICON AND TEXT"**, so the section is real and current, not archived. I could not go further to confirm all four stated layout permutations (4/3/2-tile horizontal + vertical) are actually drawn under that header — a full-page metadata crawl of this one large page felt disproportionate for a refinement pass, so I stopped at what the direct link resolves to. The only concrete visual evidence I have is the two PNGs attached to the tickets themselves (single-tile anatomy: icon/Heading/Description; and the 3-tile "Zimmermann Benefits" Cart instance) — identical attachments on both SFCC-835 and SFCC-836. Per the given ground truth, this also isn't tracked in the Figma 04.7 Component Inventory.

---

### SFCC-835 / SFCC-836 sequencing verdict

**Partial parallel, not a clean "start anytime."** The generic outer shell — grid layout for 2/3/4 tiles + vertical, empty/error placeholder, Storybook scaffold against a hand-authored stub — can start now alongside SFCC-835, consistent with this repo's Storybook/Vitest stubbing carve-out. But the icon-rendering path specifically is genuinely blocked on SFCC-835 deciding the icon field's shape (see Data axis) — that decision changes whether SFCC-836 reuses `ZimmIcon` as-is or needs a new asset-rendering path, which is not a small delta.

There's also a real inconsistency worth surfacing: SFCC-836's own text names **SFCC-835** as its content-model sibling, but SFCC-835's own text names **SFCC-317** ("Zimmermann Benefits — PWA Kit Render") as its "corresponding PWA Kit story." Neither ticket has a formal Jira issue link to the other — both only link to SFCC-316/SFCC-317. My best-supported read: SFCC-835/836 are the generic reusable schema+component pair, and SFCC-316/317 are the concrete "Zimmermann Benefits" Cart-page authoring+wiring that consumes them — but that's my inference from the pattern, not a stated fact, and it's exactly the kind of component-decomposition question that should be confirmed before a sprint locks in a dependency order.

---

### Questions to raise

1. **[BA]** Which is the real content-model↔PWA-story pairing — SFCC-835↔836 (per 836's text) or SFCC-835↔317 (per 835's text)? If it's really a four-story chain (835 schema → 836 generic component → 316/317 concrete Cart usage), worth linking that formally in Jira rather than leaving it as prose.
2. **[BA/Content]** Is the icon field a closed set matching `ZimmIcon`'s existing enum (meaning new types — truck, package, padlock — need adding to the Figma iconography spec first), or a freeform Contentful asset/SVG upload per tile?
3. **[BA/Design]** Is there an accessible-name/alt-text field per tile in SFCC-835's schema, or is the icon always decorative with the heading carrying the accessible name?
4. **[Design]** What's the mobile/responsive behaviour for each horizontal tile-count? Does it collapse to "vertical," scroll horizontally, or reflow to a grid? No mobile mockup exists in either ticket.
5. **[BA]** What should the "empty/error state" (named as in-scope by SFCC-836 itself) actually show?
6. **[Dev]** Is tile count dynamic (however many entries are linked) or a fixed authored slot choice? Affects SFCC-836's prop shape — atomic-level, dev question.
7. **[Dev]** Is this meant to register as a Contentful Experience Builder block (currently zero real components registered) so it's droppable on any page, or fetched directly by a specific page container the way `footerConfig` is today? Atomic/build-level, dev question.

---

### Readiness call

**Not ready to size with confidence yet** — PO-approved but still in Tech design with no formal AC, and the icon-asset-source gap plus the 835/836/316/317 relationship inconsistency are concrete enough to need answers before commitment; safe to start only the generic layout scaffold in parallel with SFCC-835 today.

**What I couldn't check:** whether all four layout variants are actually drawn in Figma beneath the linked header node (link only resolves to the section title); whether a separate Jira Acceptance Criteria custom field exists beyond the description (I used the field list the task specified, not `*all`); sprint/story-point fields weren't requested so I can't say whether either ticket is already slated into Sprint 5; Trello isn't connected, N/A here anyway since nothing pointed to it.
